title: K-flat total tensor represents derived bifunctor Hom
statement: Let A be an abelian category with countable products, countable coproducts, a derived category, and K-injective resolutions. Let F : A → A → A and H₀ : Aᵒᵖ → A → A be additive bifunctors with a parametrized adjunction F(P)(-) ⊣ H₀(P)(-). Use the signed product Hom totalization and sum tensor totalization of [lem-sf-weil-native-closed-forgetful]. Let H : D(A)ᵒᵖ × D(A) → D(A) have specified product-total representative isomorphisms for every complex and K-injective target, natural in both complex variables. Let W be any class of complexes such that T in W implies that Tot(F(T)(-)) preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Then for every complex P, every T in W, and Z in D(A), there are bijections Hom_D(Q(Tot(F.flip(P,T))),Z) ≃ Hom_D(Q(P),H(Q(T),Z)), natural in Z and contravariantly in both P and T. The parameter order in F and the left-first order in the displayed tensor are connected by the signed total flip.

source.place: Lemma RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective (0A96), Lemma internal-hom (08J9), and their proofs; categorical additive-bifunctor form of the same Hom-complex and localization argument.

proof.text: Curry homogeneous cochains using the parametrized adjunction, with component sign (-1)^(p*n). Check the differential and inverse identities using the signed product-Hom formula. Thus currying descends to a bijection on homotopy classes. The signed total flip converts the curried parameter-first total to the left-first total.

For T in W and K acyclic, the map K → 0 is a quasi-isomorphism, hence so is its tensor with T. Consequently the total tensor is acyclic. Transpose any map K → Hom(T,I), where I is K-injective, and transpose a null-homotopy back. This proves Hom(T,I) K-injective.

Identify maps into both K-injective targets with maps in the derived category and use the specified H representative isomorphism. Choose a K-injective representative of Z and transport the bijection along it. Naturality of currying, the signed flip and the representative isomorphisms gives the two naturality identities; arbitrary maps between K-injectives come from homotopy classes.

proof_origin.place: Proofs of 0A96 and 08J9, retaining signed totalization and representative naturality.

Mathlib supplies total flip and K-injective localization; the source supplies bifunctorHomObj and monoidal InternalHom. Existing Sheaf ringed-site lemmas are specialized to module sheaves and do not specialize to the native IsoAlgebra category. Their proofs guide the generic argument.

lean.statement:
theorem kFlatBifunctorTensorHom
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [HasCountableProducts A] [HasCountableCoproducts A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{v} A] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions A]
    (F : A ⥤ A ⥤ A) [F.flip.Additive] [∀ P, (F.flip.obj P).Additive]
    (B : CochainComplex A ℤ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (hB : B = F.flip.map₂CochainComplex)
    (H₀ : Aᵒᵖ ⥤ A ⥤ A) [H₀.Additive] [∀ P, (H₀.obj P).Additive]
    (adj : F ⊣₂ H₀)
    (H : (DerivedCategory A)ᵒᵖ × DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory A)
    (R : NativeHomRepresentatives H₀ H)
    (KFlat : ObjectProperty (CochainComplex A ℤ))
    (hflat : ∀ T, KFlat T →
      ∀ {P P' : CochainComplex A ℤ} (f : P ⟶ P'), QuasiIso f →
        QuasiIso ((B.flip.obj T).map f)) :
    ∃ e : ∀ (P T : CochainComplex A ℤ), KFlat T → ∀ Z : DerivedCategory A,
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((B.obj P).obj T) ⟶ Z) ≃
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ⟶ H.obj (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj T), Z)),
      (∀ (P T : CochainComplex A ℤ) (hT : KFlat T) (Z Z' : DerivedCategory A)
        (a : DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((B.obj P).obj T) ⟶ Z)
        (b : Z ⟶ Z'),
        e P T hT Z' (a ≫ b) =
          e P T hT Z a ≫ H.map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 _) b)) ∧
      (∀ (P P' T T' : CochainComplex A ℤ) (hT : KFlat T) (hT' : KFlat T')
        (f : P ⟶ P') (g : T ⟶ T') (Z : DerivedCategory A)
        (a : DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((B.obj P').obj T') ⟶ Z),
        e P T hT Z
            (DerivedCategory.Q.map
              ((B.map f).app T ≫
                (B.obj P').map g) ≫ a) =
          DerivedCategory.Q.map f ≫ e P' T' hT' Z a ≫
            H.map (Prod.mkHom (DerivedCategory.Q.map g).op (𝟙 Z)))
